LESSON: TRANS SAHARAN SLAVE TRADE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.3: Trans Saharan Slave Trade
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Trans Saharan Slave Trade, part of People and Relationships in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do people subject others to slave trade?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. look at a problem in a new or different way as they debate on factors that led to development of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa,

2. utilise digital technology to effectively accomplish own tasks as they use digital or print resources to research on the organization of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa, learners with manipulation

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. look at a problem in a new or different way as they debate on factors that led to development of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa,
2. utilise digital technology to effectively accomplish own tasks as they use digital or print resources to research on the organization of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa, learners with manipulation

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Trans Saharan Slave Trade together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: Learners utilise digital technology to effectively accomplish own tasks as they use digital or print

resources to research on the organization of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa.

● Creativity and Imagination: Learners look at a problem in a new or different way as they debate on factors that led to

development of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa.
